subject: Dedicated capacity: proposed validation runbook, tokens/sec & latency guarantees
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared@acme.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procure@acme.ai>
Date: 2025-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity - throughput guarantees and commit question

Hannah,

Thanks for taking the time on the call yesterday. As we scope our internal business case, procurement needs a clear picture of the throughput and latency guarantees that Redwood can commit to for a Dedicated GPU pool. High level asks from our side:

- Tokens/sec baseline per committed GPU pool and how that maps to our expected mixed workload (chat: 60%, single-turn completion: 40%).
- Requests/sec guarantees for small (<=64-token) vs. long-prompt (>=1024-token) traffic patterns.
- Latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) by model family and sequence length.
- Measurement methodology you use to validate those numbers (test harness, warm/cold cache, run length, sample size).
- How credits/penalties would be calculated if SLOs are missed.

We are also trying to lock into a 12-month reserved commit. Can you share any discount tiers tied to commit size and the burst/auto-scale behavior beyond committed capacity?

Appreciate a written summary we can attach to the procurement packet.

Best,
Jared
Director, Platform Engineering
Acme AI
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Cole <jared@acme.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-05T12:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - throughput guarantees and commit question

Jared — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise validation runbook and a pricing sheet for commit tiers (attached). Below is a summarized response and the measurement methodology we will use for contract-level guarantees. If this looks good I can turn it into an SOW addendum for procurement.

Summary of proposed guarantees (for the commit sizes in the attached pricing sheet):
- Baseline tokens/sec: we guarantee 1.2M tokens/sec per 8-GPU pool (mixed-chat-heavy profile defined below). This maps to ~1500 concurrent small requests/sec (<=64 tokens) assuming average response 80 tokens.
- Requests/sec: we guarantee 1800 reqs/sec for small requests (<=64 tokens) and 320 reqs/sec for long-form requests (~1024-token responses) per 8-GPU pool.
- Latency SLOs (within committed capacity and normal network conditions): p50 < 30ms per token, p95 < 200ms per token, p99 < 450ms per token. For long sequences the per-request latency target is: p50 < 450ms, p95 < 1200ms, p99 < 2500ms.
- Burst behavior: customers can burst up to 1.5x committed tokens/sec for short windows (up to 30 minutes/day) without additional charges; sustained bursts will draw on a reserved burst bucket billed at the overtime rate in the pricing sheet.

Measurement methodology (high level):
1) Test harness: we run a Redwood-provided harness that reproduces your traffic mix. We will provide the harness container and a seed dataset that mirrors your token-length distribution (chat vs completion).
2) Warmup and cache priming: each validation run includes a warmup period (30 minutes) to populate model KV cache and enable continuous-batching steady state. We consider the steady-state window after warmup for SLA measurement.
3) Run length and sampling: 3 independent runs each 60 minutes long, with aggregated metrics reported. We use bootstrapped confidence intervals and require the p95 to meet target in 2/3 runs for a pass.
4) Load profiles: we validate both small-request and long-request profiles and a mixed profile (60/40 chat/completion).
5) Environment: validation runs use the model variant specified in the SOW (e.g., redwood-chat-v2) on the same GPU instance types allocated for Dedicated (NVIDIA H20 class). We fix sequence padding and tokenization across runs.
6) Metrics & telemetry: token/sec, requests/sec, per-token latencies, per-request latencies, GPU utilization, batch sizes, and KV hit rate. We collect raw traces and provide a short report with percentile curves and time-series.

Credit policy for SLO misses: for any monthly window where the documented p95 (per token or per-request depending on test) misses the guarantee for more than 5% of the measurement windows, we propose a service credit equal to 10% of that month’s Dedicated invoice for each 24-hour period of non-compliance, up to a cap of 50% for the monthly invoice. Exact wording and exceptions (maintenance windows, force majeure) will be in the SOW.

Next steps: if you confirm the numbers above I will circulate a one-page validation runbook and ask Marcus to schedule an initial validation run on a non-production mirror of your workload.

Thanks,
Hannah
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Jared Cole <jared@acme.ai>
Date: 2025-10-06T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - throughput guarantees and commit question

Quick technical clarifications — looping in so procurement sees we’ve thought through the measurement artifacts.

- Token accounting: we will report tokens/sec as model-generated tokens only and include client-side tokenization details in the artifact. Prompt tokens vs. response tokens will be broken out.
- Cold-start variance: p99 can spike on model reloads. For contract validation we exclude a single reload event per 24 hours but we will log reloads and include them in the operational report.
- Mixed workloads: batching efficiency can change significantly with more short-turn chats. Our mixed-profile number is conservative (we model 60/40 with an empirically measured batching curve). We’ll attach the raw batching curve to the report.
- Measurement infra: tests need to be run from within your VPC or a controlled network path that mirrors egress; we’ll provide a runner image and a short infra checklist for your infra team.

I recommend we run an initial 60-minute mixed-profile validation and follow up with a 24-hour soak if you want to validate long-term stability (useful for large commits).

Marcus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Jared Cole <jared@acme.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme AI Procurement <procure@acme.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-08T11:44:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - throughput guarantees and commit question

Appreciate the clear summary and the runbook stub. A few follow-ups from procurement and infra: 

- Can you convert the credit policy into a short formula we can include in the procurement packet? They want something like: monthly_credit = min(0.1 * monthly_invoice * number_of_violation_days, 0.5 * monthly_invoice).
- For the burst bucket: how is burst usage tracked and reported? Does it reset monthly or daily?
- For the 1.2M tokens/sec baseline: can you show a short table mapping commit tiers (8/32/64 GPU pools) to expected tokens/sec and suggested discount band? Procurement wants to see a 3-tier map.
- Finally, we need a short clarifying paragraph for legal explaining the measurement anchors (runs, excluded maintenance, test environment parity) so they can fold it into the SOW.

If you can send those pieces we’ll attach them to the PO today and push to finalize a 12-month commit.

—Jared
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Cole <jared@acme.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-10T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity - throughput guarantees and commit question

Jared — thanks. Attaching the requested snippets in the two files we talked about (pricing sheet + validation runbook). Quick answers inline so procurement can grab text quickly: 

- Credit formula (plain text for PO/legal): monthly_credit = min(0.10 * monthly_invoice * violation_days, 0.50 * monthly_invoice). A violation_day is any UTC calendar day where the validated p95 (for the applicable metric) does not meet the guaranteed value. Maintenance windows and documented reload events are excluded.

- Burst bucket tracking: tracked at the customer level as tokens used beyond committed tokens/sec, aggregated in 1-minute windows. The bucket is sized per billing period and resets monthly at UTC midnight. Short bursts (<=30 minutes/day under 1.5x) are not billed; sustained use draws from the bucket; when the bucket is exhausted overtime rates apply. Reports will show per-minute token usage and burst charge line items.

- Commit tier mapping (text snippet for PO):
  - 8-GPU pool (base): guaranteed 1.2M tokens/sec (mixed profile). Suggested discount 10% on list price for 12-month commit.
  - 32-GPU pool: guaranteed 4.6M tokens/sec (non-linear batching gains). Suggested discount 18% for 12-month commit.
  - 64-GPU pool: guaranteed 9.8M tokens/sec. Suggested discount 25% for 12-month commit plus elevated burst bucket size.

- Measurement anchors paragraph (for SOW/legal):
  Redwood will conduct validation runs using the customer-seeded harness in a controlled environment representative of production network paths. Each validation consists of three 60-minute steady-state runs following a 30-minute warmup to prime KV caches and batching. Results are aggregated and the p95 target must be met in at least two out of three runs for a passing validation. Documented maintenance windows and unplanned reloads are recorded and excluded from violation calculations; load generators must be run from the customer VPC or an agreed-upon mirror to ensure network parity.

Next steps: I’ll convert the snippets into an SOW addendum and send to your procurement team along with the HubSpot deal link and a DocuSign for the proposed commit. Marcus will reach out to coordinate the initial 60-minute run.

—Hannah
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: dedicated_commit_pricing_v3.xlsx (pricing table, discount bands, burst rules), throughput_validation_runbook.pdf (detailed test harness and metrics collection checklist)
